newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies lower.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mixed and pork bellies lower, with December hogs supported by higher cash prices at some Midwest markets Monday, traders said.
Fund selling was featured in pork bellies, which traders said appeared to be profit-taking.

In hogs, traders said selling throughout the session appeared to be profit-taking after a four-cent gain since October 23. CME December hogs peaked Monday at 56.45 cents per lb versus the October 23 high of 52.45.
Futures traders said cash hogs may trade steady to lower Tuesday, which discouraged aggressive buying of the nearby futures. Also, talk circulated that cash pork prices may be edging lower.
At midday Tuesday, USDA reported cash loin prices were weak, hams steady to $2.00 per cwt lower and pork bellies $1.00 to $2.00 lower.

Pork belly futures closed lower, but within last week's trading range. Commission houses Lind Waldock, Paine Webber and Refco sold February bellies lower, and the rest of the session consisted of light volume selling, traders said.
Although stored bellies can now be delivered against the February, traders said Monday's selling did not appear to be by hedging interests.
Hogs closed down 0.525 to up 0.125 with December up 0.050 at 55.950. Pork bellies were down 1.125 to up 0.450 with February off the most at 69.475.
